review_scope: Complete 114-line model-access procedure and three one-line reusable artifacts read. Organization/team modes, union semantics, app scope, preview migration and rollback retained. Dependencies previously reviewed are not duplicated; linked team creation and actual settings remain unverified.

claims.statement: Declared scope is the Copilot cloud feature and Business/Enterprise plans, administered by enterprise owners; neither metadata nor navigation verifies actual permissions.
Enterprise-wide enabled/disabled settings form a baseline; granular organization delegation and opt-in enterprise-team control are distinct modes.
Default organization mode permits organization decisions and enterprise targeted rules; these are separate control paths.
Enterprise-team granular control is explicitly an opt-in preview, not generally enabled state.
The procedure recommends explicit enterprise-wide decisions for universally allowed or forbidden models, delegating only granular access; example cost/compliance choices are not adopted policy.
Enterprise access, AI-controls and Copilot sidebar includes are navigation dependencies, not authorization or completed configuration.
Enterprise model statuses distinguish Enabled for all users/apps, Disabled for all users/apps and delegated organizational or team/app decisions.
Agent-app model access is a separate reusable dependency whose default installation scope changes in enterprise-team mode.
Unconfigured models use Delegate to Default Policy; an enabled default policy makes them available to everyone, while explicit disabling or scoped delegation can limit access.
Organization instructions apply only outside the enterprise-team preview; delegated unconfigured organization models inherit that organization's released-model default policy.
Targeted organization rules select organizations and allowed models before creating the rule; the procedure does not independently specify conflict ordering between multiple targeted rules.
Opting into enterprise-team mode deactivates organization-level model settings and removes organization owners' model-policy management.
Preview rollback restores the pre-opt-in policy state and discards later enterprise-level model-policy changes; recovery must capture both states rather than assume preservation.
Enterprise-team grants are additive but cannot re-enable a model disabled at enterprise level.
Enterprise-wide enabled models remain enabled for teams; team settings are not a deny override.
A user's effective team allowance is the union of enabled models across all memberships plus enterprise grants; one enabling team suffices.
Team settings have no explicit Disabled option; delegated models default to Optional, meaning not currently enabled for that team, not an overriding deny.
The preparation recommendation is to recreate and enhance organizational access using enterprise teams before opting in; training or cost examples do not establish actual eligibility.
Prepared team default-model settings do not take effect until preview opt-in.
Enterprise-wide explicit Enabled/Disabled choices persist at opt-in, but organization-delegated models become unavailable until enabled for specific teams; migration can cause access regression.
The procedure calls for filtering delegated models and choosing teams; the linked team-creation article remains independently unreviewed through this reference.
The enterprise-team-mode toggle is a documented opt-in action; no actual toggle or protection change is performed by this review.
Team grants require the enterprise model status Delegate to Enterprise Teams/Apps, then enabling selected models on the team's Default models tab.
Agent apps are separately described and require delegated enterprise-team/app status for app-specific model grants.
App model configuration changes Optional to Enabled for each chosen model through Configure app models; app allowance is distinct from membership allowance.
The supported-surfaces reference limits interpretation of policy coverage; linking it is not evidence of client enforcement.
Configure models is the navigation action for model availability; opening a configuration view does not enact policy.
By default agent apps inherit models enabled in their installation organization or personal account; enterprise-team mode instead controls app models at enterprise level.
Agent apps are partner-built GitHub Apps exposing delegated agents alongside the cloud agent and other third-party agents; this classification does not establish trust, permissions or model access.
